trace.title: Configuration and variables
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Terraform describes resources through providers and tracks managed identity in state. Configuration is desired structure; state maps that structure to actual remote objects.

A plan compares the chosen inputs/state/provider view with reality and proposes changes.

State can contain sensitive values. Use a deliberate backend/access/locking/recovery strategy.

Two uncoordinated applies can race. Manual console changes create drift that must be understood before the next plan.

Learning setup: use a dedicated training configuration, pin provider/tool versions, review variables and account/region, run formatting/validation, inspect a saved plan, and apply only when you deliberately choose the real resource/cost changes.

The course does not run apply or create AWS infrastructure.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Configuration + variables + state + provider context → plan → human/team review → apply → refreshed state → observed service.

A successful apply proves resources changed, not that Rails works end to end.

Before a replacement/destruction, inspect why the provider proposes it and which data/lifecycles are affected. Keep backups and recovery separate from state-file backups.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
State is not an application database backup. Removing a resource block can propose deletion.

A plan from the wrong account/variables is the wrong plan even if syntactically valid.
